answer: The protocol weaves a trellis of time‑locked stakes: each new agent must post a cryptographic bond that vests its reward in a linear sonnet of epochs, and the bond’s size is calibrated to the current juniper‑priced compute cost. As epochs pass, only a fraction of the reward unlocks, so a sybil farm can earn at most a trickle while still paying the full upfront bond each time it spawns an identity. The attacker’s expense therefore scales linearly with the number of identities, quickly exceeding any profit from the slow vesting stream.
